unitTitle: Describing Location - Relative Pronouns - Relative Adverbs - Some/Any/No

pairsWith.noteUz: Bu nazariya beti Coursebook 12-unit (Holidays with a Difference) grammatikasini takrorlaydi: joylashuv, nisbiy olmoshlar, some/any/no va hosilalari.

scanNote:
GRAMMAR 2, 12-UNIT NAZARIYA (58-bet, PDF 57). Yuqorida chapda ko'k '12', sarlavha: 'Describing Location - Relative Pronouns - Relative Adverbs - Some/Any/No'. Och pushti ramka, ikki ustun.

CHAP USTUN:
'Describing Location': • To describe the location of a place we can use the following phrases: ... is situated/located in the east/west/south-east, etc of; on the north/south/south-west coast of, etc; in the heart/centre of ... 'Vancouver is situated on the west coast of Canada. The art gallery is located in the heart of the city.'
'Relative Pronouns': • Relative pronouns (who, which, etc) introduce relative clauses. We use relative clauses to identify the noun in the main clause. 'I met a woman. She's from France. I met a woman who is from France. (relative clause)' (The relative clause identifies which woman we are talking about.) • We use who to refer to people. 'A porter is someone who carries luggage.' • We use which to refer to objects or animals. 'A clock is something which shows the time.'
'Relative Adverbs': • We use where to refer to place. 'This is the hotel where we spent our holidays.'
'Some - Any - No': • We use some, any, and no with uncountable nouns (cheese, coffee, etc) and plural countable nouns (houses, eggs, etc). 'some cheese, some houses' • Some means a little or a few. We normally use some in positive statements. 'She's got some bread. (= a little) She's got some pencils. (= a few)' • We can also use some in questions to make offers, requests, or when we expect a positive answer. 'Would you like some more orange juice? (offer)' • We use any in questions and not any in negations. 'Have you got any milk? No, I haven't got any sugar.'

O'NG USTUN:
• We can use no instead of not any in negations. 'They haven't got any money. They've got no money.' JADVAL: Countable/Uncountable - Affirmative: some; Interrogative: any; Negative: not any/no.
'Someone/Something/Somewhere': • Someone/Somebody (a person), something (a thing) and somewhere (in/to/at a place) are used in positive statements. 'There is someone in the kitchen.' • Anyone/anybody, anything and anywhere are used in questions and negations. 'Is there anything in the box? There isn't anybody in the room.' • No one/nobody, nothing and nowhere can be used in negations instead of not anyone/anybody, not anything and not anywhere. 'There isn't anybody in the garden. There is nobody in the garden.' JADVAL: People - someone/somebody, anyone/anybody, not anyone/no one, not anybody/nobody; Things - something, anything, not anything/nothing; Places - somewhere, anywhere, not anywhere/nowhere. Who? someone/anyone/no one, somebody/anybody/nobody. What? something/anything/nothing. Where? somewhere/anywhere/nowhere.

Bet raqami: pastda chapda '58'.

exercises.instructionUz: Joyning o'rnini tasvirlash uchun quyidagi iboralar ishlatiladi: ... is situated/located in the east/west/south-east of (... ning sharqida/g'arbida/janubi-sharqida); on the north/south/south-west coast of (... ning shimoliy/janubiy qirg'og'ida); in the heart/centre of (... ning markazida). Vankuver Kanadaning g'arbiy qirg'og'ida joylashgan. San'at galereyasi shahar markazida joylashgan.
exercises.explanationUz:

  LOCATED.

  IN the east / west / south-east
    OF ... (... ning sharqida)
  ON the north / south coast OF
    ... (... ning qirg'og'ida)
  IN the heart / centre OF ...

  Vancouver IS SITUATED ON the west
  coast OF Canada.
  The art gallery IS LOCATED IN the

⚠ 'THE HEART OF THE CITY':

  = shahar yuragi (markazi).


⚠ 'ON THE COAST' - qirg'oqda;
  'IN THE EAST' - sharqda.

She's from France. → I met a woman who is from France. (The relative clause identifies which woman we are talking about.) We use who to refer to people: A porter is someone who carries luggage. exercises.instructionUz: Nisbiy olmoshlar (who, which) nisbiy ergash gapni boshlaydi. Nisbiy ergash gap bosh gapdagi otni ANIQLAShTIRADI: Men bir ayolni uchratdim. U Fransiyadan. → Men Fransiyadan bo'lgan ayolni uchratdim. (Qaysi ayol haqida gapirayotganimizni aniqlaydi.) 'Who' - odamlar uchun: Yuk tashuvchi - yuk ko'taradigan odam. 'Which' - narsa va hayvonlar uchun: Soat - vaqtni ko'rsatadigan narsa. Nisbiy ravish: 'where' - joy uchun: Bu biz ta'tilni o'tkazgan mehmonxona.
exercises.explanationUz:
NISBIY OLMOShLAR - IKKI GAPNI
  BIRLAShTIRADI.

  I met a woman. She's from
  France.
  → I met a woman WHO is from
    France.
  (qaysi ayol? - Fransiyadan

  WHO   → ODAM:
    A porter is someone WHO
    carries luggage.
  WHICH → NARSA / HAYVON:
    A clock is something WHICH
    shows the time.
  WHERE → JOY (nisbiy ravish):
    This is the hotel WHERE we

⚠ O'ZBEKChA:

  Nisbiy gap o'zbekchada '-gan'
  sifatdosh bilan beriladi: 'yuk
  ko'taradigan odam', 'ta'tilni
  o'tkazgan mehmonxona'.


⚠ 'A PORTER':

  = yuk tashuvchi (mehmonxona,
  vokzal).

sections.title: Some - Any - No / Someone - Something - Somewhere
sections.titleUz: Some - Any - No / Someone - Something - Somewhere

exercises.instructionEn: We use some, any, and no with uncountable nouns (cheese, coffee) and plural countable nouns (houses, eggs): some cheese, some houses. Some means a little or a few. We normally use some in positive statements: She's got some bread. (= a little) She's got some pencils. (= a few). We can also use some in questions to make offers, requests, or when we expect a positive answer: Would you like some more orange juice? (offer). We use any in questions and not any in negations: Have you got any milk? No, I haven't got any sugar. We can use no instead of not any in negations: They haven't got any money. = They've got no money. Someone/somebody, something, somewhere - positive statements: There is someone in the kitchen. Anyone/anybody, anything, anywhere - questions and negations: Is there anything in the box? There isn't anybody in the room. No one/nobody, nothing, nowhere - negations instead of not anyone, not anything, not anywhere: There isn't anybody in the garden. = There is nobody in the garden.
exercises.instructionUz: Some, any va no sanalmaydigan (cheese, coffee) va ko'plik sanaladigan (houses, eggs) otlar bilan: some cheese, some houses. Some = bir oz / bir nechta; odatda TASDIQ gapda: Uning bir oz noni bor. Uning bir nechta qalami bor. Some SAVOLDA ham - taklif, so'rov yoki 'ha' javobini kutganda: Yana apelsin sharbati ichasizmi? (taklif). Any - SAVOLDA, not any - INKORDA: Sut bormi? Yo'q, shakar yo'q. Inkorda not any o'rniga NO: Ularda pul yo'q. Someone/somebody, something, somewhere - TASDIQDA: Oshxonada kimdir bor. Anyone/anybody, anything, anywhere - SAVOL va INKORDA: Qutida biror narsa bormi? Xonada hech kim yo'q. No one/nobody, nothing, nowhere - INKORDA not anyone/anything/anywhere o'rniga: Bog'da hech kim yo'q.
exercises.explanationUz:
SOME / ANY / NO.

  TASDIQ:  SOME  - She's got SOME
           bread.
  SAVOL:   ANY   - Have you got
           ANY milk?
  INKOR:   NOT ANY = NO
           They haven't got ANY
           money. = They've got NO
           money.

  ⚠ Taklif/so'rovda SOME (savol
  bo'lsa ham): Would you like SOME
  more juice?


HOSILALARI (jadval):

            TASDIQ     SAVOL/INKOR  INKOR
  ODAM:     someone    anyone       no one
            somebody   anybody      nobody
  NARSA:    something  anything     nothing
  JOY:      somewhere  anywhere     nowhere

  There is SOMEONE in the kitchen.
  Is there ANYTHING in the box?
  There isn't ANYBODY in the room.
  = There is NOBODY in the room.

  ⚠ 'nobody / nothing / nowhere'
  bilan fe'l TASDIQDA (is, not
  isn't): 'There ISN'T nobody' ✗.


⚠ Who? → someone / anyone / no one
  What? → something / anything /
    nothing
  Where? → somewhere / anywhere /
    nowhere

patterns.formula: JOY + is situated / located + on the ... coast of / in the heart of ...
patterns.exampleEn: Vancouver is situated on the west coast of Canada.

patterns.formula: OT + is someone who / something which / the place where + ...
patterns.exampleEn: A porter is someone who carries luggage. A clock is something which shows the time.
patterns.exampleUz: Yuk tashuvchi - yuk ko'taradigan odam. Soat - vaqtni ko'rsatadigan narsa.

patterns.formula: There is someone ... / Is there anything ...? / There isn't anybody ... = There is nobody ...
patterns.exampleEn: There is someone in the kitchen. Is there anything in the box? There is nobody in the garden.
patterns.exampleUz: Oshxonada kimdir bor. Qutida biror narsa bormi? Bog'da hech kim yo'q.

groups.ruleUz: ⚠ SOME- / ANY- / NO- + ONE / BODY / THING / WHERE
